title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 358–359 of the 'équation des lacets' notes, continuing La Longue Marche). Grothendieck studies an automorphism u of the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, or of an extension of it. Throughout, σ_∞ is an involution of π̂_{0,3} and ρ is the order-3 rotation of the three punctures. The data attached to u are:
- a 'multiplier' μ, with ν = (μ−1)/2. This is the cyclotomic exponent, i.e. Drinfeld's λ and m = (λ−1)/2.
- an element f, determined only modulo L_0 = ℓ_0^{Ẑ}.
- two defects g and h, measuring the failure of u to commute with ρ and with σ_∞.

The 'loop relation' (11) is σ_∞(h)·g = σ_∞(f)^{-1} ℓ_1^ν ρ(f). It is a reformulation of the hexagon-type relation for (λ,f) in what was later called the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.

Cocycle step (previous page). The equations '(2)' are cocycle conditions for the Z/2-action via σ_∞ and the Z/3-action via ρ. They are solved as coboundaries: h = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} with β ∈ π̂_{0,3}, and g = αρ(α)^{-1} with α in an extended group π̂_{0,3}·{1,τ_∞}. In modern terms this is a computation of nonabelian H^1(Z/2, ·) and H^1(Z/3, ·) with coefficients in π̂_{0,3}.

On this page:
1. Substituting into (11) gives relation (15): σ_∞(βσ_∞(β)^{-1})·(αρ(α)^{-1}) = σ_∞(f)^{-1} ℓ_1^ν ρ(f).
   - ν is uniquely determined by (α,β), and f is determined in L_0\π̂_{0,3}.
   - The right-hand side is unchanged under f ↦ ℓ_0^n f, n ∈ Ẑ.
2. Grothendieck states the 'principal dissymmetry' between σ_∞ and ρ:
   - the σ_∞-cocycle h always trivializes inside π̂_{0,3};
   - the ρ-cocycle g trivializes inside π̂_{0,3} (α ∈ π̂_{0,3}) iff ν ≡ 0 mod 3, i.e. μ ≡ 1 mod 3.
   - In cohomological terms: the class of g in H^1(Z/3, π̂_{0,3}) is trivial iff μ ≡ 1 (3).
3. Normalization. Applying formula (12) with γ = β^{-1}, the inner-twisted automorphism u' = int(β^{-1})u has:
   - g' = β^{-1}gρ(β) = (β^{-1}α)ρ(β^{-1}α)^{-1};
   - h' = 1;
   - f' = fβ.
   So every u is conjugate modulo inner automorphisms to one commuting with σ_∞. The next page adds that this u' is unique, and that the symmetric normalization (commuting with ρ) is possible only when μ ≡ 1 (3).

What the page serves: normalizing GT-type automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} up to inner automorphisms, and identifying the cohomological obstruction to a ρ-equivariant normalization.
errors: No mathematical error found. Formula (16) checks out from (12) with γ=β^{-1}: h' = β^{-1}βσ_∞(β)^{-1}σ_∞(β) = 1, g' = (β^{-1}α)ρ(β^{-1}α)^{-1}, f' = fβ.

The claim 'α ∈ π̂_{0,3} iff ν≡0 (3)' is asserted ('on le voit') without proof on this page. It presumably follows from abelianizing (11) and the ρ-cocycle condition mod 3, but this is not written out.

The invariance of the right-hand side of (15) under f ↦ ℓ_0^n f implicitly requires that σ_∞(ℓ_0)^{-1}…ρ(ℓ_0) cancels appropriately (i.e. compatibility of ℓ_0 with ℓ_1^ν under σ_∞ and ρ). This is not verified here.

ideas.what: Expressing the defects g, h of an automorphism u as nonabelian coboundaries g=αρ(α)^{-1}, h=βσ_∞(β)^{-1}, and rewriting the loop (hexagon-type) relation as a relation among α, β, f, ν
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological interpretation of the GT relations (nonabelian H^1 of Z/2, Z/3 acting on F̂_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, 'A cohomological interpretation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group' (Invent. Math. 1997); Drinfeld 1990 for GT itself
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as known; unsure

ideas.what: Dissymmetry: the σ_∞-cocycle always trivializes in π̂_{0,3}, while the ρ-cocycle trivializes iff μ≡1 mod 3 (ν≡0 mod 3)
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction in H^1(Z/3, F̂_2) to ρ-equivariant normalization of GT elements; λ mod 3 condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (related discussion in Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps)

ideas.what: Normalization u' = int(β^{-1})u commuting with σ_∞, unique up to inner automorphisms, with f' = fβ
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of GT elements so that f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 (2-cycle relation)

missed.claim: Grothendieck (c. 1981, before Drinfeld's GT) already treats the loop relation as a nonabelian cohomology problem for the Z/2 and Z/3 symmetries of π̂_{0,3}. He isolates the asymmetry that the σ_∞-cocycle always trivializes while the ρ-cocycle trivializes iff μ ≡ 1 mod 3.
missed.quote: La dissymétrie principale ... entre σ_∞ et ρ dans cette théorie, c'est que l'on a toujours β ∈ π̂_{0,3}, tandis que α n'est pas nécessairement dans π̂_{0,3} - il l'est ... ssi ν ≡ 0 (3) i.e. μ ≡ 1 (3).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the Lochak–Schneps cohomological interpretation of GT. It also gives an explicit criterion (λ ≡ 1 mod 3) for when a GT-type element can be conjugated to commute with the order-3 symmetry. That criterion is a clean statement worth checking against the literature on GT normalizations; I am unsure it is recorded there in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The cohomological reformulation of the hexagon relation is known (Lochak–Schneps 1997), and the normalization by σ_∞ is standard. What is notable is that Grothendieck had this framing early and stated an explicit mod-3 obstruction for ρ-normalization. That detail is plausibly not credited to him, but it is probably known to GT specialists in some form.
transcription_corrections: In (15) the right-hand side should read σ_∞(f)^{-1} ℓ_1^ν ρ(f), not 'h^ν', matching (11) on the previous page.
'f est déterminé dans \widehat{π_{0,3}}' should read 'f est déterminé dans L_0\π̂_{0,3}'.
'la deuxième rel. de (15)' is likely 'le deuxième membre de (15)' (the right-hand side).
'changement de f en h^n f' should be 'ℓ_0^n f', consistent with the previous page's f ↦ ℓ_0^n f.
'l'on a toujours β ∈ \widehat{π_{0,3}}' should read β ∈ π̂_{0,3} (the non-extended group), contrasting with α in the extended group.
